newsitem.title: UK: Charity calls for end to illegal U.S. bear hunts.
newsitem.headline: Charity calls for end to illegal U.S. bear hunts.

text.p: About 40,000 bears are illegally killed in the United States every year, many of them by cruel, "unsportsmanlike" methods, a British-based animal rights group said on Wednesday.
The World Society for the Protection of Animals (WSPA) said in a report that there was growing demand for bear hunts to satisfy the tourist industry and the trade in Chinese medicines.
It said its researchers had found more than 50 operations willing to arrange bear hunts for British tourists.
The hunters often used tactics which have been outlawed in many states.
"Bears are hunted with a variety of weapons, ranging from modern rifles to bows and arrows and even muskets," the WSPA said. "The methods are cruel and unsportsmanlike."
One of the most common practices is known as "hounding", where dogs chase a bear until it is exhausted and takes refuge in a tree.

The dogs wear radio transmitters so the hunter need only wait until the animal stops moving before following behind to shoot it and throwing it to the dogs, whichi rip it to pieces. The practice is legal in 19 U.S. states.

In the U.S. presidential election on November 5, voters in five states will decide in a referendum whether to ban bear hunts by hounding or by two other methods opposed by the WSPA, spring hunts and baiting.
In baiting, bears are lured with food to sites where the hunters wait to shoot them at point blank range.
In spring hunts, the bears are shot when they emerge from hibernation with their cubs to forage for food. Often only the parent is shot, leaving the cubs orphaned.
"WSPA is calling on voters to outlaw these cruel and unecessary forms of hunting," the group said.
In addition to the 40,000 bears killed illegally each year, 40,000 are legally hunted the WSPA said.
It said 75 percent of the world's bears live in North America. There are around 650,000 black bears and 65,000 brown bears in the U.S. and Canada.
